name: Facet
text: Use a horizontal timeline strip at the top, fixed height, always visible. This keeps the main view uncluttered while ensuring users never lose context of the timeline. The trade-off is less vertical space for other content, but clarity and speed of scanning outweigh that cost.

name: Pane
text: Fixed-height strips bury critical detail when users zoom into dense data—users lose precision. A collapsible, resizable strip with a "focus mode" toggle may introduce complexity users won’t tolerate. Settle it by testing both against a task: can users identify the exact event in a crowded timeline faster with either approach?
